newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans ends up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans ends up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on continued short-covering from retail investors, but trading was slow due to the approach of the weekend, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,325 yuan ($401) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at 3,325 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,318 and a high of 3,326.
March, May and July did not trade, November rose one yuan to 3,331, the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,340.
Combined volume fell to 21,300 tonnes from 22,400.
Traders said most institutional investors stayed on the sidelines with the approach of the weekend.
"Retail investors were the main force on the market with most institutions having little interest in trading due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
A second trader said he expected soybeans to remain dull as many investors found other markets, such as the share market, ($1=8.2955 yuan)
